inputs.original_text: Tom Homan hasn’t ruled out immigration enforcement at polling places, and the real question is why Democrats seem so alarmed by the possibility that the law will be enforced. Voting should be orderly and lawful; no one should be above ordinary enforcement simply because an election is underway. The administration’s mixed messages have caused confusion, but that is no reason to make election integrity and the rule of law taboo.
inputs.modified_text: Tom Homan hasn’t ruled out immigration enforcement at polling places, and that should not be treated as some untouchable subject. Elections must be orderly and lawful, and nobody should get a pass from ordinary law enforcement because voting is taking place. Democrats’ alarm only raises a fair question: why frame the enforcement of the law as a threat? The administration’s mixed messages have created confusion, but the answer is clarity—not making election integrity taboo.
